m.intro: Digital Footprint Counter estimates, it does not measure. This page explains how, with which data, and where the estimates are weak. Every number in the dashboard comes from the formulas and coefficients below.
m1.title: 1. How activity is detected
m1.body: The extension observes the requests the browser makes (domain and, when the server declares it, the response size) and which tab is active. Active time is counted for the focused tab while you are not idle, and for tabs playing audio. It never reads page content, full URLs, prompts, cookies or passwords: only the domain is kept, locally.
m2.title: 2. What information is actually available
m2.body: Available: domain, number of requests, bytes declared by the server (Content-Length) and active time. Not available: server consumption, the type of content, or whether a request to an AI service is a chat message or an image generation. HTTPS traffic is encrypted, and when a server does not declare a size the request counts as 0 bytes and the reliability is lowered.
m3.title: 3. How each operation is classified
m3.body: Domains are matched against a local catalogue (data/catalog.json); the most specific match wins. Domains not in the catalogue stay in 'Other' with low reliability. Visiting an AI site is classified but never assumed to be a generation.
m4.title: 4. How local, network and remote consumption are estimated
m4.body1: Local device: energy = active hours × device power. It depends on time only.
m4.body2: Network and data center: energy = gigabytes × kWh/GB for ordinary browsing. For streaming it is hours × kWh/hour, and for AI services it is hours × assumed usage rate × energy per operation. Each component uses one driver only (time or bytes) to avoid double counting.
m4.body3: Conversions: CO₂e = energy × grid carbon intensity; water = energy × litres per kWh; cost = energy × electricity price. Energy (Wh) is stored; the three metrics are computed when displayed, so changing the region recalculates the history.
m4.body4: Local processing time is not accessible to extensions and is not measured: it is covered only through the device power assumption.
m5.title: 5. Coefficients applied
m5.hint: Each coefficient has a range, a status and its sources. 'Assumption' and 'To verify' values are listed in docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md.
m6.title: 6. Sources
m7.title: 7. Margins of error
m7.body: Every result is a range: the minimum uses all the lowest coefficients, the maximum all the highest. It is an envelope of documented uncertainty, not a statistical confidence interval. Reliability levels:
m8.title: 8. What cannot be measured
m8.item1: The actual consumption of remote servers for each request.
m8.item2: Whether an AI request is a conversation or a generation, and which model answered.
m8.item3: Remote energy of AI video generation (no reliable coefficient yet).
m8.item4: Traffic and activity outside the browser, and the embodied energy of devices.
m8.item5: Local processing time of web pages.
m8.item6: Resources whose servers do not declare their size.

welcome.title: Your browsing has a footprint.
welcome.lead: See it, understand it, reduce it. Estimated privately, on your device.
welcome.step1.title: Pin the leaf
welcome.step1.body: Extensions menu (puzzle icon), then pin. Your day at a glance.
welcome.step2.title: Choose your region
welcome.step2.body: Sets electricity mix and price. Change it anytime.
welcome.step3.title: Just browse
welcome.step3.body: The leaf turns green, yellow or red. Click it for the dashboard.
welcome.privacy: Only domains, counts, bytes and time are kept, on this device. Never content, addresses or prompts.
